result:
The proposed answer is very likely wrong, though I'm relying on recalled literature rather than a full derivation.

The proposed solution claims, with no justification, that the maximal graphs are exactly C₃ and P₄. These two are plausible members of the family of H with bounded clique-width, but the claim that they are maximal is doubtful.

The known results on induced minors (Belmonte, Otachi and Schweitzer) say that excluding H as an induced minor gives bounded clique-width exactly when H is an induced subgraph of the gem or of co-(P₃+2K₁). The gem is P₄ plus a dominating vertex, and it contains both C₃ and P₄ as induced subgraphs. Excluding an induced subdivision is a weaker restriction than excluding an induced minor, so the family of valid H for subdivisions is smaller, and its maximal graphs would be larger than C₃ and P₄ only if some bigger graph qualifies. I could not confirm which graphs qualify.

A further problem is that the solution asserts the maximal set without checking any larger candidate. Several graphs with more than 4 vertices, such as the paw, diamond, or gem, could be maximal. Also, if the maximal set contained only C₃ and P₄ (each with 3 edges), the sum would be 6, which looks suspiciously like a guess rather than a derived value.

Because the solution gives no derivation and conflicts with the structure of the known induced-minor result, I do not accept it.

VERDICT: REJECT
